readings.summary: Add a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] attribute for partial formatter classes where the generator emits a contractless (public members only) formatter for T, honouring any MessagePack attributes already on T, with no surrogate or key-mapping mechanism.
readings.code_difference: Attribute has no SurrogateType or key-configuration property; generator treats T with no [MessagePackObject]/[DataContract] as contractless and fills in the IMessagePackFormatter<T> implementation in the annotated class.

readings.summary: Add the attribute with a SurrogateType (or similar) parameter so a type in Project B mirrors T's members and supplies keys/unions, with the generated formatter mapping between them.
readings.code_difference: Attribute exposes a SurrogateType property; generator reads a surrogate type's attributes/keys by property name and emits conversion code between surrogate and T, which the contractless-only reading would not do.

data.quote: For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.
